atomicity.reason: One obligation (exclude invalid-flagged samples from limit evaluation); the all-invalid sentence is an edge case of the same rule.

comprehensibility.reason: The obligation is intelligible without the limit table's contents; the invalid flag and limit table are named descriptively.

feasibility.reason: A per-sample flag check before comparison is trivial and contradicts nothing else stated.

parent_fit.reason: ARCH_SAFETY_SUPERVISOR states it ignores measurements tagged invalid; this requirement turns that into the testable rule that such samples can never produce a limit-violation event.

unambiguity.reason: One reading: any sample with the flag set is skipped, and the all-invalid cycle case is stated explicitly rather than left to inference.

verifiability.reason: A concrete test can feed samples with the invalid flag set at values beyond every limit and assert that no limit-violation event is emitted.

summary: Full marks on the rubric. Flagging for the stage (not scored against this need): unconditional exclusion of invalid samples leaves an unbounded protection blind spot for a stuck-invalid channel, and no swreq in this set bounds how long a channel may stay invalid.
